newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended slightly lower after a dull Monday, with trading very quiet due to a partial U.S. public holiday.
A powerful dollar supported the peseta, which ended stronger although dealers were ruling out bigger gains.
"Today was a day to forget," said Emilio Sainz at Natwest in Madrid, "but we still have a market not far from its all-time record high and I feel the positive trend resuming soon".
The March future contract hit a high at 114.98.
But others were worried by forex and EMU jitters.

"Dollar strength, which used to support peripherals in the past, doesn't any more," said Valentin Fernandez at Credit Lyonnais in Madrid. "People buy dollars because they fear a weak euro, and the more likely it is Spain and Italy will enter EMU, the more likely it is we'll have a stronger dollar".
But he added that forex volatility, considered the factor keeping the Bank of Spain off cutting rates, is putting pressure on the three-year bond.
Natwest's Sainz said "We had a drastic flattening in the yield curve, but I see it as stop-loss selling and I think now is less risky than it used to be.
